newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Airbus announces new aircraft orders.
newsitem.headline: Airbus announces new aircraft orders.

text.p: The European Airbus Industrie consortium said on Tuesday it had sold or agreed to sell a series of aircraft for delivery between 1998 and 2000.

Airbus said in a statement received in Singapore that German charter carrier Condor would purchase 12 A320 passenger aircraft with an option for another 12 planes of the A320 family. The planes would replace the carrier's Boeing 737 fleet for routes within Europe.
All the ordered A320s would be delivered to Condor between 1998 and 1999. The engine selection for this order was still pending, it said.
Airbus said cargo company Federal Express had ordered 11 additional A300-600 freighter aircraft for delivery between 1998 and 2000.

Airbus said the new Federal Express aircraft would be powered by General Electric CF6-80C2 engines and used primarily on domestic routes in the United States. Federal Express previously ordered 25 A300-600Fs in 1991, it said.

A separate Airbus statement said Hong Kong-based Cathay Pacific Airways had signed a contract to purchase three more ultra long-range A340-300s, increasing to nine the number of firm orders placed by the airline for the four-engine aircraft.
The newly ordered aircraft would be delivered during the second and third quarters of 1998 and would operate between Hong Kong, and Europe and North America.
The Airbus statements gave no financial details. They did not explain why the announcements had been made in Singapore.
Airbus officials were not immediately available for comment.
